question.text: Per the chapter, the book value per share is normally considered which of the following?

answer.text: The ceiling price above which equity cannot be valued
The floor price or least value attributable to a going-concern business
The fair market value for all going concerns

explanation.text: The Logic: Quoted: 'Book value of share... is normally considered the floor price or the least value attributable to a going concern business which is expected to continue in business in future.' The Trap: Book value is neither a ceiling nor always equal to intrinsic nor fair market - it is a floor. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C, XXI-B and X-B test this floor-price concept.
